in_hebrew.name: יולנדה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'yolanet' meaning 'jewel, precious one'. This name is not directly found in the Bible, but it is derived from the biblical name Esther, which means 'star, or hidden treasure'. Yolande can be seen as a variation of the biblical name Esther.

in_greek.name: Ιολάνδη
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'iole' meaning 'violet' and 'andros' meaning 'man' or 'mankind', thus 'violet one'. In Greek mythology, Iolande was the name of the nymph Iole, who was beloved by Zeus. This name is not directly mentioned in the Bible, but it can be seen as having biblical connections through Greek mythology and the biblical name Esther.

in_latin.name: Iolanda
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'iolus' meaning 'jewel' and 'andreia' meaning 'manliness, bravery', thus 'jewel and manliness'. This name is not directly mentioned in the Bible, but it can be seen as having biblical connections through the Latin word 'iolus' and the biblical name Esther.
